title: Cost of the LCFs' meaning: how much of the seven LCFs a linear map reads from the free latents
description: For each free encoder of exp-lcf-cost-teacher-317 (lcft-freefix-none-sN, the clone of BBRv3 whose encoder every lcft-freefix policy of seed N keeps, and the eight lcft-freeslow policies) and the free arm's configuration chosen in exp-lcf-cost-search-316 (both seeds, exp-lcf-cost-315), a least-squares map with a bias from the seven latents to each of neto1 v1's LCFs, in neto1 v1's target space, fitted on the training links of the policy's own split of exp-data-net2-steps-222 and scored by R^2 on its validation links, every 10th step (experiments/latent_probe.py). References: neto1 v1's own output (the paper arm's latents) and the free encoder with fresh weights. probe.md has the table.
run: N="$IN/n/$(cat "$IN/n/chosen.txt")/net1.pt"; A=(); for d in "$IN"/t/lcft-freefix-none-s* "$IN"/t/lcft-freeslow-*; do A+=("$(basename "$d")=$d"); done; for c in lcf-paper-c0.1-lr1e-4-n60k-s0 lcf-free-c0.01-lr1e-4-n60k-s0 lcf-free-c0.01-lr1e-4-n60k-s1; do A+=("$c=$IN/p/$c"); done; [ "${#A[@]}" -eq 13 ]; uv run python experiments/latent_probe.py "$OUT" "$IN/d" "$N" "${A[@]}" random=random
